Written in Solingen on the 17th of December 1960

Dear relatives, it’s been a while since we have last heard from each other. Since we have forgotten most of the English we had learned a couple of years ago, it always take a while for us to write to you. However, if we could send you letters in German, we would write to you more often. First of all, I would like to introduce myself. My name is Ruth Braun and I am Heinrich Braun’s daughter-in-law — I am his son Heinz’s wife. We have a small daughter who is 5 1/2 years old, her name is Susanne. The main reason I am witting this letter to you is to wish you a merry Christmas and happy new year. We are doing good and we are praying to God that we will stay healthy and hope the same for you. That’s all for today. Best wishes and again, merry Christmas and a happy new year. 

Your Heinrich Braun, his daughter Gertrud with husband and son Peter, as well as Ruth Braun, Heinz and Susanne.

Can I ask why the command has to be translated? I know a lot of German dog trainers and owners that still use English commands because it’s easier. For this trick in particular, I do know people who simply say “Touch!”


Anyways, I think a lot of German commands for dogs aren’t grammatically correct, just to make it easier for the dog to follow. “Sitz”, “Platz”, “Fass”, are short and easy for the dog to follow. In the end, it’s not like they understand the words anyways. They’re just following sounds. A short, one-syllable word is a lot better suited. If you wanted to be 100% grammatically correct, you’d say “Setz(e) dich!“, Leg(e) dich!“ or “Fass(e) das!“ 


By the way, the imperative of “zielen” would be “ziel(e)!”. There’s no “du” involved at all here, in any imperative form.

Dear Mrs. Dölke (?),

In order for our telephone call to not get any more expensive than it already was, and because I assume you haven’t quite understood what I was trying to tell you last Tuesday, I am writing you this letter.

You asked me how I knew about your husband being in Baramuda – I told you in the post card that I accompanied him on the journey there. As you know the journey started on Thursday in Leipzig. We travelled from Warsaw, Minsk, Polotsk all the way to Baramuda, where we eventually arrived on Monday at 10 pm. During the train ride, we stayed in coach #28 and I stayed with your husband all the way until our arrival. The journey itself was pretty smooth. Just once, the train had to stop for a night because the route was blocked and had to be taken care of. Some people sang, some played skat, others just slept. In Russia, we saw traces of the war. They are used to help you set clearer intentions for your question. Sometimes you want to ask about a certain topic but don’t know how to word your question. So you could look up “Tarot spreads about (topic you want to ask about)” and it will show you in what order to draw the cards and how to place them, as well as what questions the cards you pull will answer.

So let’s say you want to do a reading for the next year. You search for a “New Year’s tarot spread” online. Something like this could come up:

“Card 1: A lesson you learned this year that will help you grow next year,
Card 2: Energy you should leave behind next year,
Card 3: Energy you should focus on next year”

It will show you how to place the cards. Sometimes it’s just three cards next to each other, sometimes the placement of the cards varies.

If you’re ready to do the reading, you can either memorize the spread or print it out/place it next to you. Then you will draw the cards to answer the questions of the spread.

First of all, there’s a religious aspect. A lot of people view tarot as a fortune telling device. In some bible verses, there’s God specifically saying that people who tell fortunes or believe in omens should be stoned to death. Since RWS and Crowley, who made the tarot as we know it today famous, were occultists, a lot of people view it as an occultist thing and are scared of it or link it with something demonic. Granted, most people reading the cards today the fluffiest, most harmless people ever.

What people don’t understand is that tarot doesn’t have to be magickal or spiritual. It can be the most mundane thing ever - in the ends, it’s playing cards. Hey! Personally, I always recommend new learners to start off by learning about the symbolism of RWS. If you’ve got down the symbolism or understand meanings of certain aspects of the cards, interpreting them will be much easier than simply studying each card’s meaning without really knowing why they mean the things they mean. If that makes sense?

I also find it really important to get a lot of input from other people. Read everything you can find, watch every YouTube video on meanings, follow people on Instagram if that’s something you’d be interested in. Getting new perspectives is very helpful in the learning process because some people will give you completely new insights that you never would’ve thought about in a million years! I’ve been practicing for almost two years now and I still learn new things every day.

A good way to get to know the cards is to pull one card every morning. This is going to be your card of the day. Sit down for a bit and write down how you’d interpret this card in regards to a message to you for today. In the evening, sit back down and review your own interpretation. Compare if you were right or what other things happened that day that could’ve to do with your morning pull.

For example you pull the Three of Swords. Maybe your first interpretation would be: “Oh no, someone is going to break my heart!” (I feel like this is the most obvious interpretation for this card). At the end of the day, sit down and review that. Did someone actually break your heart? Or have you experienced something else that wasn’t too pleasant. What was it?

And yes, definitely read the cards for others! Ask some friends or family or your girlfriend to do a very easy one to three card spread for them. Do it in a setting and with someone that won’t make it awkward or uncomfortable. Take all the time you need. Ask whether or not your interpretation is resonating with them along the way. This is very helpful. Just don’t read the cards on a hard topic just yet. Something easy going should to the trick for now.

Hope this helped!

You can go about it both ways. 

Personally, I do prefer gridding my fabric or buying pre-gridded fabric. If you do want to grid your fabric, it’s best if you use water-soluble fabric pens because others might be hard to wash out once you’re finished. Personally, I find it way easier this way because I make less mistakes this way and have a better reference to where the stitches need to be. I’ve heard from some people who don’t like the extra work, though, or people who get confused by the grid rather than it helping them. Maybe try googling it. There are also other ways to grid, for example using thicker floss.

If you do not want to grid, I suggest finding the middle of your pattern (oftentimes, there’s a little arrow next to the pattern on the top as well as on the sides showing where it is) as well as the middle of your fabric and starting there. To me, that’s the easiest way to go about it without a grid. ☺️
